tei:titleStmt.tei:title: [Gebet] Am Laubhüttenfest beim Kreisgang mit dem Lulaw und Esrog
[Prayer] on Sukkot at the Haḳafot with the Lulav & Etrog, by Fanny Neuda (1855)

tei:div.tei:head: [Gebet] Am Laubhüttenfest beim Kreisgang mit dem Lulaw und Esrog

tei:lg.tei:l: And circle your altar, O Eternal One.” (Psalms 26:6)

Lord of the Universe, You have richly adorned nature with Your gifts and blessings. The valley with its lush greenery, the mountain with its crown of forests, the field with its bountiful harvest—all are the fruit of of your grace, for the blessing of your children, for the nourishment of their bodies, to satisfy their needs, to delight their eyes, and as a balm for their wounds; and no leaf is so small, no blade of grass so low in the vast realm of nature, that it does not contain soothing, healing powers for us. The humble shrub and the majestic tree, the fragrant rice and the golden fruit—all call out to us: “Praise, O son of the earth, the almighty Lord who has created such wonders; praise, child of man, your heavenly Father, who so graciously provides for you!” – And with praise, honor, and thanksgiving, we take up this festive bouquet—these four kinds of nature’s produce, this small reflection of the earth’s rich diversity, this herald of Your omnipotence and goodness, O God, and lift it up and turn it toward all corners of the world and the heavens; for everywhere, in all the ends and corners of the world, your blessing grows and springs forth for us; and singing your praise, we circle your altar with it.

Yes, Lord, it is not only our mouths that should give thanks to you, nor only our lips that should sing your praise; but through deeds of piety and love, we wish to honor and worship you. Just as you lovingly bestow gifts upon us, may we remember the poor among us with kindness and compassion; just as you graciously grant us days of blessing and joy, may we bring joy and a festive spirit to the hearts of the needy through refreshing gifts. Let this be our thanksgiving, our festive offering, which may you graciously accept from us. Amen.
